newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares waver on Dow slide but buyers seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares waver on Dow slide but buyers seen.

text.p: Leading Russian shares opened at a new record on Tuesday, and while traders said profit taking on alarm over Monday's slide on Wall Street hit some shares in early trade, they saw continued support for the market to close.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened at 401.34, or 0.19 percent higher than Monday's record 400.59 closing.

The Dow Jones index fell 192.25 points, or 2.5 percent, on Monday to close at 7604.26. It was the second biggest single-day point loss in Dow history after the Black Monday 508-point drop on October 19, 1987.

"Russia does not correspond directly to the U.S. market, but such things do not escape the notice of traders," said Alfa Capital deputy head of sales Alexei Genkin. "But now prices are going up and there are buyers."
National power company UES ticked up to $0.3450 at 0830 GMT from $0.3420 on Monday, after sinking to $0.3380 just after the market opened.
Regional power company Krasnoyarskenergo fell to $0.407 from $0.435 but trade was thin.
Krasnoyarskenergo shareholder Rossiisky Kredit Bank said on Monday the energy company's main production asset, Krasnoyarsk hydroelectric station, had voted to separate from the company.
Oil company LUKoil LKOH.RTS jumped to $18.80 from $17.99.
"There is still strength left in LUKoil and UES," said one trader at a Western brokerage. He saw the market as a whole remaining strong despite the morning correction.

"It's not sustainable, this downward movement," he said of opening uncertainty. "I think there's still a lot of people waiting on the sidelines with money (to invest) before they take off for a long August vacation."
